subject: System Design
title: How Twitter Scaled the Timeline
description: A fast breakdown of How Twitter Scaled the Timeline for builders.

hook.text: A user with 50 million followers tweets. Delivering that tweet to 50 million timelines is a massive problem.

buildup.text: Twitter first used a pull model: query all followed accounts when loading the timeline. It was too slow.

discovery.text: They switched to fan-out: when you tweet, it's pre-written into all followers' cached timelines.

twist.text: Celebrities broke fan-out. 50 million writes per tweet was too expensive. They use a hybrid approach.

climax.text: Twitter's timeline is fan-out for most users, pull for mega-celebrities. A blend of both strategies.

punchline.text: No single approach works at every scale.

quiz.question: Why did Twitter switch from pull to fan-out for timelines?
options: Querying all followed accounts on every load was too slow
Pull wasn't supported by their database
